narrative.overview:
OurGiti presents itself the way a well-run system looks from the inside: a set of frosted glass panels, each reporting that something is in good order, resting over soft green light. The register is the category standard for premium technology companies (the user benchmarked Stripe, Vercel and Cloudflare), executed straight and at full craft: sentence-case headlines set tight and slightly wide, generous space, white and soft green-gray grounds by day, near-black green by night, and one emerald green that carries every action in both schemes.

The proof is shown, not photographed. Every visual is product-style UI built in markup (the hero's valley scene of a business and its systems, a bookings app, a network, a support queue, a cloud checklist) with illustrative values and a caption that says they are illustrative. Glass appears only where there is colour behind it to frost: the header over the page, the hero scene's labels over the landscape, the Process walkthrough, the layers of the one deep-green band, and the contact card. Depth is quiet: hairline borders, one soft offset shadow, a lit 1px edge. Motion is a single orchestrated entrance in the hero and a 2px lift on cards; nothing else moves.

The system replaces the rejected 2026-11 "Engineering Pad" world, which must not return (see Do's and Don'ts). Missing company facts are shown as missing, in a dashed "Coming soon" pill, never filled with stand-ins.
keyCharacteristics: Light and dark are equal citizens: every colour is a `light-dark()` pair, and green is the brand in both.
One emerald green for every action; status amber and red live only inside UI visuals and error messages.
Frosted glass over soft green light, used only where something sits behind it.
Product-style UI visuals built in code, captioned as illustrative; no photography, no illustration.
Mona Sans for everything, set tight and slightly wide; Geist Mono only for data.
Pills for actions and states, 16px rounded rectangles for containers.

rules.name: The One Green Rule
rules.body: Emerald is the only accent. Every action, link, focus ring and selected state is green; amber and red appear only as status inside UI visuals and as form errors. No second brand hue, ever.

rules.name: The Paired Scheme Rule
rules.body: Every colour is written once as a `light-dark(<light>, <dark>)` pair on `:root, .inverse`; `html.light` and `html.dark` pin a scheme, otherwise the system setting applies. Never write a scheme-specific override for a single component.

rules.name: The Scheme Flip Rule
rules.body: A subtree that flips its scheme must also re-declare the tokens: `.inverse` sets `color-scheme: dark` and is listed in the `:root, .inverse` token selector, because Tailwind's Lightning CSS compiles `light-dark()` into variables that resolve where the custom property is declared. Any future flipped subtree joins that selector; setting `color-scheme` alone does nothing.

rules.name: The Data-Only Mono Rule
rules.body: Geist Mono is for data: times, counts, statuses, values and the URL inside the UI visuals, plus the process step numerals, which are an ordered index. Labels inside visuals are Mona Sans 12.5px muted. Mono never sets a heading, a label, a button or running copy.

rules.name: The Sentence-Case Rule
rules.body: Headlines are sentence case, end with a period, and are set in weight 600 with negative tracking. No all-caps, no letterspaced labels, no condensed faces anywhere.

rules.name: The Light Behind Glass Rule
rules.body: Glass is used only where there is colour behind it to frost: the header over the page, the hero scene's small labels over the landscape, the Process walkthrough over the lit section, the layers inside the deep-green band, and the contact card over a light field. Glass on a flat white ground is just a grey box; use a card.

rules.name: The Solid Sheet Rule
rules.body: A surface nested inside glass cannot frost what is behind its parent, so it is solid. The mobile menu sheet under the glass header is `surface` with the Glass shadow, deliberately opaque.

rules.name: The Lift-On-Response Rule
rules.body: Cards rest with the Rest shadow and gain the Lift shadow, a firmer border and a 2px rise only on hover. Nothing floats at rest except glass.

dos: Do write every new colour as a `light-dark()` pair on `:root, .inverse`, and add any new scheme-flipping subtree to that selector (the Scheme Flip Rule).
Do keep emerald the only accent: primary fills in Emerald Signal, green text and icons in Legible Emerald, tints in Emerald Wash.
Do put glass only where there is colour behind it, and give every glass surface the solid `glass-solid` fallback for reduced transparency and missing `backdrop-filter`.
Do make a panel nested inside glass solid (`surface` with the Glass shadow), as the mobile menu sheet is.
Do show work as product-style UI built in markup, with illustrative values and a caption that says so.
Do keep Geist Mono to data inside visuals (times, counts, statuses, values, URLs) and the process numerals; set labels in Mona Sans 12.5px muted.
Do use pills for actions, chips and states, and 16px rounded rectangles for containers.
Do keep a chip's icon slot filled ("+" unselected, check selected) at a constant text weight.
Do render a missing fact as the dashed "Coming soon" pill, and disable any action that depends on it, without its arrow and with a plain note.
Do keep motion to the hero assembly (rise 14px, frost from blur(0), fill always present) and the 2px card lift, all instant under reduced motion.
donts: Don't reintroduce the rejected 2026-11 "Engineering Pad" world: graph-paper grounds, hand-drafted sketches, all-caps condensed type (Barlow Condensed), GIVEN / FIND / SOLUTION worksheet wording, pale-green paper or a lime highlighter.
Don't add a second accent hue, gradient text, or neon glows on black; amber and red are status colours inside visuals only.
Don't let light fields become shapes: they stay low-alpha radial light (0.13 and under at night), masked out before the section edge, behind glass, never hard-edged or animated.
Don't use stock photography (handshakes, people at laptops, blue server rooms), illustrations, mascots or bouncy motion.
Don't put glass on a flat ground with nothing behind it, or nest a translucent sheet inside glass.
Don't start the hero panels invisible or fade them in from zero opacity.
Don't set headings, labels or buttons in all-caps, letterspaced or condensed type, and don't set labels in mono.
Don't place a label above a headline; a section opens on its sentence-case headline.
Don't add a border to a well inside a card, or nest boxes in boxes.
Don't number items unless their order carries information.
Don't invent contact details, clients, figures, certifications or response times to fill a gap.
Don't reuse the provisional wordmark mark (tile and orbit) as a motif; it will be replaced by the logo.
